nutshell: The Inland Empire (Riverside and San Bernardino counties, 4.8M people, 27,000 square miles) has one of the thinnest Anglo-Celtic trad scenes of any big US metro: about 13 verified recurring jams, sessions, open mics and dances, roughly 40 meetings a month. There is one Irish session (a biweekly, snowbird-season lunch session at a Palm Desert golf course), three bluegrass jams, no contra, no old-time jam, no shape-note singing and no fiddlers' association district. The biggest scheduled trad dance form is modern club square dancing, under the Cow Counties Hoedown Association. Look past fiddles, though, and the region has one of the most distinctive living traditions in any US metro: Cahuilla bird singing. Revived from near-extinction in the 1980s, it now fills a festival of its own in Palm Springs, opens every regional powwow, and in 2022 opened Coachella. Around it are a national-champion youth mariachi, a 50-year-old folklórico company, Basque Chino, a century-old Californio fiddle band at the Ramona pageant, and the ghost of a 1970s bluegrass festival boom (Norco, Calico, Huck Finn) that has since moved into LA County or faded. For contra, Sacred Harp or a weekly session, IE players drive west to Claremont and beyond.

venues.name: Pappy & Harriet's Pioneertown Palace
venues.notes: A former Western movie-set cantina in Pioneertown (founded 1946 by Roy Rogers, Gene Autry, the Sons of the Pioneers and others). It was 'The Cantina' biker burrito bar from 1972, then Pappy & Harriet's from 1982. Robyn Celia & Linda Krantz owned it 2003-2021; it now belongs to Morgan Margolis & partners (Knitting Factory Ent.). It is the desert's main Americana/roots room, with 3 of the 4 Coachella-area folk listings on nwfolk.com's calendar for Nov-Dec 2026.

festivals.name: Calico Ghost Town Spring Bluegrass Festival / Calico Bluegrass Festival (2026: 'Spring Jam')
festivals.notes: Organized in the 1980s by Don Tucker, who claimed 10,000-12,000 per year in 1988 and 24,000 in the 1976 Bicentennial year. It had fiddle, banjo, guitar, band and clogging contests ($2,500 in prizes in 1988) (https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-05-07-vw-2460-story.html). The County Parks page for the 2024 edition lists Americana bands at $15 adult (https://parks.sbcounty.gov/event/calico-bluegrass-festival-2/). The 2025 edition was May 10. The 2026 schedule calls it 'Spring Jam' (May 9): 'live bluegrass music and hands-on animal fun'. The attendance figure is the 1988 midpoint claim.

The 2025 edition was Nov 22 at the Joshua Tree Cultural Center (https://joshuatreevoice.com/gramfest-2025-brings-cosmic-american-music-back-to-joshua-tree/).

heritage_traditions.tradition: Cahuilla bird singing (and Serrano/Cupeño/Luiseño bird songs)
heritage_traditions.community: Cahuilla bands (Agua Caliente, Morongo, Torres Martinez, Cahuilla/Anza, Santa Rosa, Cabazon, Los Coyotes), Serrano (San Manuel, Morongo)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Revived from near-extinction in the 1980s by elders (Robert Levi, Anthony Andreas Jr., Alvino Siva) with a California Arts Council grant; now sung at Singing the Birds (2,500+ attendees), Malki Kewet, every regional powwow, fiestas, funerals and all-night sings. Tribal chairman Thomas Tortez Jr. estimated 200+ bird singers across Santa Rosa, Agua Caliente, Cabazon and Morongo alone. Full cycle is 300+ songs.

ACTA: Ernest Siva is 'the last living Paa'chucham singer'; learned from a 1970s recording of Lloyd Marcus singing the last 12 songs; taught grand-nephew Isaac Horsman Rodriguez in a 2008 ACTA apprenticeship.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Mojave (Kwatsaan) bird songs and bird dancing
heritage_traditions.community: Fort Mojave Indian Tribe, Needles (San Bernardino Co.)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Bird singing competition at the 50th Fort Mojave Indian Days (Oct 2025) and 2026 contest; youth bird dancing; touring Rez Life Bird Singers.
groups: Aha Macav Avi Kwa Ame Bird Singers

heritage_traditions.tradition: Peon (hand game) and its gambling songs
heritage_traditions.community: Southern California tribes (Cahuilla, Serrano, Luiseno and others)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Morongo's 2026 powwow schedule lists Peon for men, women, boys and girls at dusk on Saturday, alongside the bird singing and dancing contest. Not researched further.

heritage_traditions.community: Chemehuevi Indian Tribe, Havasu Lake (San Bernardino Co.); Southern Paiute
heritage_traditions.evidence: Sacred funerary song cycle revived by the Salt Song Trail Project co-founded by Matthew Leivas Sr. (Chemehuevi) and Vivienne Jake (Kaibab Paiute).

heritage_traditions.community: Pan-tribal; boarding-school and urban Native communities
heritage_traditions.evidence: At least five large annual powwows: Morongo (35th in 2026, 30,000+), San Manuel at CSUSB (since 1996), UCR (43rd in 2026), Sherman Indian HS (40th in 2026), Pechanga (24th in Jan 2027). Most add a bird-singing segment, a local twist.

Riverside Arts Academy's Mariachi Campana de Riverside won the 2026 Mariachi Nationals (Anaheim) after 3rd at Tucson; CSUSB Mariachi Los Coyotes; UCR mariachi/son jarocho courses (MUS 175A/B); Lake Elsinore Mariachi Fest (6th in 2026); Indio Mariachi Festival.
Ballet Folklorico de Riverside founded 1976 by Ana de la Tejera (50th year in 2026); Mi Lindo Mexico (Rialto) and many school groups perform at Riverside Day of the Dead.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Dia de los Muertos (altars, danza azteca, folklorico, music)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Riverside Day of the Dead Festival, 23rd annual in 2025, 'tens of thousands' across seven blocks of Market St and White Park; began with ~200 people.

heritage_traditions.tradition: P'urhepecha (Purepecha) danza de los Ancianos / Viejitos, pirekua, patron-saint fiestas
heritage_traditions.community: P'urhepecha migrants from Michoacan (Ocumicho), Eastern Coachella Valley (Mecca, Duros and Chicanitas camps on Torres Martinez land)
heritage_traditions.evidence: David Bacon (2011): young people rehearse la Danza de los Ancianos every December to guitars and horns for the Guadalupe procession to the church in Mecca; ~5,000 Purepecha in the eastern valley at peak; Facebook page 'Cultura Purepecha Pirekuas - CPP' (Coachella) ~21,700 followers; Purhepechas Unidos del Valle de Coachella active Nov 2025.
groups: La Comunidad Purepecha del Valle de Coachella
Purhepechas Unidos del Valle de Coachella

heritage_traditions.evidence: Has accompanied the Ramona outdoor play since 1924; repertoire 'has not changed in nearly 90 years' (2011); fourth generation performing; residency at the Mission Inn late 1950s-1960s. Freshest independent evidence 2014; current participation not confirmed.

Only academic traces found: UCR mariachi courses 'emphasize mariachi and son jarocho'; UCR Gluck son jarocho workshops. No recurring public IE fandango found (the strong SoCal fandango scenes are in LA and Santa Ana).

heritage_traditions.tradition: Basque (pelota, Basque dance, Klika drum-and-bugle, mus, Basque picnics)
heritage_traditions.community: French-Basque dairy and sheep families, Chino
heritage_traditions.evidence: Two clubs: Southern California Basque Club (founded 1946; 80th picnic + NABO convention July 2026) and Chino Basque Club (1968; ~150 members, 10 events/yr, Labor Day picnic; dance groups Xori Ttipiak, Eskualdun Izarrak, Dantzari Onestak); Centro Basco boarding house/restaurant since 1940; Bidart family fronton.
56th season in 2026; convention center built in 1976 in the shape of a tent as its permanent home; German bands including acts from Germany.

heritage_traditions.community: Scottish Society of the Inland Empire
heritage_traditions.evidence: Small society (~255 Facebook followers) that sends members to Scottish Fest USA (Costa Mesa, Orange Co.) rather than hosting its own games; no IE highland games found.
groups: Scottish Society of the Inland Empire

heritage_traditions.evidence: Senryu Taiko founded 1998 with Prof. Deborah Wong, 'one of the earliest intercollegiate taiko groups'; 17th annual spring concert 2025. No Obon/Bon Odori found inside the MSA.

heritage_traditions.community: African American, San Bernardino Westside, Riverside
heritage_traditions.evidence: Churches dating to 1911 (New Hope Missionary Baptist) and St. Paul AME; Riverside Juneteenth community choir sing (2025-26). Community gospel as a 'folk' scene is under-documented online.

Once the West Coast's center of gravity (Calico 1976: 24,000; Huck Finn Jubilee IBMA Event of the Year 2001); Huck Finn left the MSA in 2022 and paused in 2026; Calico shrank to a one-day festival; Blythe's Desert Bluegrass Festival continues (March 2026).
Calico Days (Old West reenactment with bands) 59th-60th annual; Pioneertown (1946 movie set) now home to Pappy & Harriet's; Temecula Rodeo Oct 2026. No cowboy-poetry gathering found in the MSA.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Filipino, Korean, Vietnamese, Hmong, Armenian, Dutch (Chino), Irish, Obon
heritage_traditions.evidence: Rich history (Filipino-led Coachella grape strike, May 3 1965; Pachappa Camp, first Korean settlement on the US mainland, 1905) but no living music/dance practice could be verified in the MSA for these communities in 2024-26. Treat as 'not found', not 'absent'.

people.name: Robert Levi Sr.
people.notes: Torres Martinez; Sherman Institute alumnus and staff, sax and clarinet player, WWII veteran; formed the Intertribal Cahuilla Bird Singers; recorded a 5-CD set of Desert Cahuilla bird songs; won a California Arts Council grant to train young singers incl. San Manuel's James Ramos. Died Aug 2007 at 89.

people.name: Anthony J. 'Biff' Andreas Jr.
people.notes: Brought bird singing back to Agua Caliente; sang at the Andreas Ranch, UCR fundraisers, parades. A web-search summary claiming an NEA Heritage Fellowship (1995) for 'Anthony Andreas' is FALSE: he is not on the NEA's California list.

people.name: Alvino Siva
people.notes: Los Coyotes Cahuilla/Cupeno, 'the last Cahuilla Indian cowboy'; student of Joe Patencio; led his own group; died June 26, 2009 in Banning.

people.name: John Joseph (Joe) Patencio
people.notes: Teacher of Alvino Siva and Anthony Andreas; 'was told not to carry these songs on'.

people.name: Ernest H. Siva
people.role: singer, music educator, founder of Dorothy Ramon Learning Center
people.era: living (born and raised on Morongo Reservation)

people.name: Bill Madrigal Sr.
people.notes: ACTA master artist 2002 (apprentice Sean Bogner); teacher of Gerald Clarke.

people.name: Luke Madrigal

people.name: Gerald Clarke
people.notes: Cahuilla Band (Anza); led the 2023 Singing the Birds; learned from Bill Madrigal Sr. and Alvino Siva; prefers 'all-nighters' with the full cycle.

people.name: James Ramos
people.notes: Trained by Robert Levi; first Native American elected to the California State Assembly; has sung bird songs before the Legislature.

people.name: Matthew Leivas Sr.
people.role: Salt Song singer, co-founder Salt Song Trail Project

people.notes: NEA lists him as of Cathedral City; moved to the desert in 1973 to front a club in Rancho Mirage and settled in Palm Desert in 1974. The only NEA Heritage Fellow found with an IE residence.

timeline.event: Spanish expedition passes Pahsitnah, a large Native settlement on the ridge at today's Ramona Bowl; smallpox later scatters survivors toward Soboba.

20-30 New Mexican families (incl. genizaro/Indian-Mexican ancestry) found Agua Mansa and La Placita de los Trujillo on the Santa Ana River, the first non-Native settlements in the San Bernardino Valley and the largest between New Mexico and LA in the 1840s.
437 Latter-day Saints from Salt Lake found the San Bernardino colony (to 1857).
Perris Indian School opens; moves to Riverside as Sherman Institute in 1902 (school band photographed c.1901).
Pachappa Camp, the first Koreatown on the US mainland (c.300 people), founded in Riverside by Dosan Ahn Chang Ho.
New Hope Missionary Baptist Church, oldest Black Baptist church in San Bernardino, opens.
Lucile Hooper records Cahuilla songs (incl. a 'Bird Song' by Allejandro) on wax cylinders, now at UC Berkeley's Hearst Museum.
First Ramona pageant at the Ramona Bowl, Hemet (April 13).
Jose Arias and his Troubadours begin playing early California music for Ramona, a family tradition into a fourth generation.
'Ramona' (Mabel Wayne / L. Wolfe Gilbert), the first song written as a movie theme, becomes a hit for Gene Austin.
Centro Basco opens in Chino as a boarding house for Basque dairymen and sheepherders.
Southern California Basque Club founded; Pioneertown movie set built for Roy Rogers and Gene Autry westerns.
Pioneertown founded as a living Western movie set; Idyllwild Arts Foundation (ISOMATA) founded by Max & Bee Krone
Swing Auditorium (10,000 capacity) opens at the National Orange Show, San Bernardino.
ISOMATA's first summer session in Idyllwild
'California Annual Champion Fiddlers Contest & Square Dance Festival' at the Farmers Fair of Riverside County, Hemet (Sept 7-8).
Pal Recording Studio opens in Cucamonga (Zappa's Studio Z from 1964).
Malki Museum founded on the Morongo Reservation; Kewet fiesta revived in 1966 after 20 years, ~5,000 attend.
May 3: Filipino grape pickers (AWOC, Larry Itliong) strike in the Coachella Valley, prelude to the Delano strike.
Golden Ring folk cafe opens in Claremont (just outside the MSA)
KUCR goes on air
Chino Basque Club founded at the Pyrenees Bar.
Big Bear Lake Oktoberfest begins (56th season in 2026).
Dick Tyner's first Golden West Bluegrass Music Festival in Norco with Bill Monroe and Lester Flatt; Gram Parsons dies at the Joshua Tree Inn (Sept).
First Golden West Bluegrass Festival, Norco, with Bill Monroe and Lester Flatt; Gram Parsons dies in Joshua Tree
Joe Patencio, Agua Caliente song keeper, dies; a young Stuart Duncan meets Pat Enright at the Calico festival.

Bicentennial Calico Ghost Town bluegrass festival draws 24,000; Tucker family founds Huck Finn Jubilee; Ballet Folklorico de Riverside founded; Roy Rogers-Dale Evans Museum moves to Victorville; Big Bear builds a tent-shaped Oktoberfest hall.
Calico festival claims 24,000 attendance; Huck Finn Jubilee founded (date disputed)
Harriet and Claude 'Pappy' Allen open Pappy & Harriet's Pioneertown Palace.
Pappy & Harriet's opens
c.1980s: Cahuilla bird singing, near extinction, revived by elders mentoring youth with a California Arts Council grant (exact year not found).
UCLA ethnomusicology students record Cahuilla bird songs (Edith Johnson, Brenda Romero, Gail Schwartz).
LA Times describes a SoCal spring circuit led by IE festivals (Calico, Norco, Huck Finn)
Huck Finn Jubilee books the Osborne Brothers and turns to national acts.
Lalo Guerrero (Cathedral City) named NEA National Heritage Fellow.
San Manuel Pow Wow begins; Gram Fest (Cosmic Americana Music Festival) runs at Joshua Tree 1996-2006.

Huck Finn Jubilee named IBMA bluegrass event of the year

Joshua Tree Music Festival begins
Robert Levi dies (Aug 29, aged 89); Alvino Siva and Anthony 'Biff' Andreas Jr. die in 2009.
Don Tucker dies; Huck Finn moves to Cucamonga-Guasti Park, Ontario (2013-16); Riverside Arts Academy founded.

Synthesis: about 13 verified recurring trad/folk events (~40 meetings/month) in a 4.8M metro; Huck Finn Jubilee (now in San Dimas, LA Co.) pauses for 2026; Calico's festival becomes 'Spring Jam'; Mariachi Campana de Riverside wins the Mariachi Nationals; Morongo powwow draws 30,000+.

costs.notes: No contra and no house-concert series found inside the MSA. Jams, the Palm Desert session (buy lunch) and the Back to the Grind open mic are free. Square-dance class $7 (Sunkissed). ECD $5 (unverified). Folk Music Center open mic $3 and concerts $10 (outside MSA). Calico festival $15 adult (2024). SWBA SuperJam $10/car day use, $20/night dry camping. Riley's Colonial Faire $18-22.

surprises: The region's signature living tradition isn't fiddling but Cahuilla bird singing: a line of men with palm-seed gourd rattles, women dancing as one body, and a 300+ song migration cycle sung dusk to dawn. It nearly vanished by the 1980s; in 2023 the Torres Martinez chairman counted 200+ singers in just four sister bands.
Coachella opened in 2022 and 2023 with a Cahuilla bird-song land acknowledgment, and some bird singers refused to take part: 'not to glorify what we're doing. It's for our people.'
A metro of 4.8 million has exactly one Irish session: biweekly, October to April, Saturday lunch at a Palm Desert golf course, mixing Irish, Scottish, Cape Breton and Norwegian tunes.

There is no contra dance, old-time jam, shape-note singing or CSOTFA fiddlers' district anywhere in the two counties. In 1970 the Southern California Old-Time Fiddlers' Association declined to join the state association and then split into old-time and 'amplified country and Western' factions.
The most-scheduled trad dance form is modern club square dancing, coordinated by the 'Cow Counties' Hoedown Association, named after the 19th-century nickname for these ranching counties.

The region's oldest continuous fiddle lineage is Californio: the Arias Troubadours' twin violins have played the Ramona pageant in Hemet since 1924, with a repertoire that 'has not changed in nearly 90 years'.

The IE was once SoCal's bluegrass festival capital. Golden West in Norco brought Monroe and Flatt in 1973, Calico Ghost Town drew 24,000 in 1976 (where 8-year-old Stuart Duncan started playing festivals), and Huck Finn in Victorville was IBMA Event of the Year in 2001. Huck Finn has since moved to San Dimas (LA Co.) and paused for 2026, and Calico's festival was renamed 'Spring Jam' in 2026.

P'urhépecha migrants from Ocumicho, Michoacán rehearse the Danza de los Ancianos each December in trailer camps on the Torres Martinez Cahuilla reservation, then process to the church in Mecca: one Indigenous people's dance on another's land.
Mojave bird songs at Needles were partly borrowed from the Cahuilla as the Mojave's own creation songs faded (Llewellyn Barrackman, Bancroft finding aid).
Chino, now a warehouse suburb, still has two Basque clubs (1946 and 1968), a family fronton, a Klika drum-and-bugle corps and an irrintzi (Basque yell) contest.
Riverside's youth Mariachi Campana won the 2026 Mariachi Nationals. A claim that it was the 'first California ensemble ever' to win was retracted the next day.

AI search summaries confidently named a Cahuilla bird singer a 1995 NEA Heritage Fellow. The NEA's own list has exactly one IE-resident fellow, Lalo Guerrero (1991, Cathedral City), the 'father of Chicano music'.
Big Bear built a convention center shaped like a beer tent in 1976 just to house its Oktoberfest, now in its 56th season.
LA's shape-note group domain, still linked from the national directory, now redirects to a gambling spam site, so IE singers following the directory hit a dead end.
curiosities: Is the IE's density of about 8 recurring trad events per million residents per month the lowest of the 20 metros? Is the 'bedroom metro' effect (players commute to LA/OC/Claremont jams) visible in other exurban MSAs?

Do other metros have a revived Native song genre with its own festival (like Singing the Birds) rather than only powwows? Compare Phoenix (O'odham waila, Yaqui), San Diego (Kumeyaay bird songs) and Seattle (Coast Salish).

Why did the 1970s-2000s bluegrass festival belt (Norco, Calico, Victorville) leave the IE: organizer deaths, county-park policy, heat, or an aging audience? Did Phoenix-area festivals (e.g. Wickenburg) follow the same arc?

Do retirement and snowbird metros (IE, Phoenix, Tampa, Orlando) sustain modern club square dancing and senior international folk dance better than young metros, and do their sessions show the same Nov-Apr seasonality as Palm Desert?
Is school mariachi the real folk-instrumental pipeline in Latino-majority metros? Which cities' youth programs win Mariachi Nationals (Riverside vs San Antonio vs Tucson vs Phoenix)?
Why no contra or ECD revival in a metro with UC Riverside, the University of Redlands and Cal State San Bernardino? What did Sacramento or Phoenix have that the IE lacks?
Are there other century-old pageant bands like the Arias Troubadours (Santa Barbara Fiesta, San Gabriel's Mission Play), and is the Arias family still playing Ramona in 2026?
Do Basque communities elsewhere (Boise, Reno, Bakersfield, San Francisco) show the same two-club split and picnic calendar as Chino?
Why is there no Obon inside the IE when LA County has about 16 each summer? Where do IE Japanese-American families dance?
What did ISOMATA's 1950s Idyllwild folk workshops actually contain, and did they feed the LA revival?
Does 'mythic site' tourism (Gram Parsons in Joshua Tree, Pioneertown) ever produce participatory music, or only listening? Compare Okemah and Clarksdale.
Has the Calico contest tradition (fiddle, banjo, guitar, band and clogging, $2,500 in prizes in 1988) moved anywhere, or does SoCal now have no public fiddle contest south of Fullerton?
data_quality_notes: Web search was heavily rate-limited (several research threads shared a quota), and Facebook, Instagram and Meetup were mostly unreadable, so jams and clubs organized only on social media are probably undercounted, especially in Hemet/Menifee, the High Desert and the Coachella Valley. The Cow Counties Hoedown member roster is JavaScript-only, so square dancing in the retirement towns is undercounted. The Southwest Bluegrass Association site blocks fetches (a June 2025 Wayback capture was used). The Riverside ECD (englishcountrydancing.org, 1st/4th Sundays) has a live but undated site and is NOT counted. The Temecula and Yucca Valley bluegrass jams are low confidence. Sources disagree on Huck Finn's founding year (1974/1976/1977/1978) and its move to Ontario (2013 vs 2014). Calico attendance figures are 1988 organizer claims. Purépecha material is mostly 2011-2019 journalism, and the Arias Troubadours at Ramona are confirmed only to 2014. Annual heritage events are prorated at 1/12 a month in recurring_events_per_month_total. The NEA check scanned all 53 California fellows on arts.gov. No Library of Congress/AFC field collections from the IE were found by API search. Son jarocho, Oaxacan, Filipino, Vietnamese, Hmong, Armenian, Dutch and Obon traditions were NOT FOUND, which is not proof of absence. No dedicated acoustic/folk instrument shop or folk luthier was verified inside the two counties (the functional folk shop is Claremont's Folk Music Center, in LA Co.). Claremont and San Dimas items are flagged outside_msa and belong to the LA count. Overlap with LA: the Back Abbey session, Folk Music Center open mic and Claremont Israeli dance appear in both files; count them only for LA.
